newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond primary market to see healthy volume.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond primary market to see healthy volume.

text.p: The U.S. corporate bond markets are expected to receive a healthy amount of new supply this week, although at a more modest level than last week, syndicate sources said.
This week's calendar for junk bonds includes roughly $2.5 billion in new paper, a reduction from last week's heavy calendar which included over $4.5 billion in new deals.
Investment-grade corporate bond supply this week is expected to consist of a handful of medium-sized offerings.
"It will be quieter than last week," said one sydnicate official. "There is nothing earthshattering coming up."
This week's largest deal may be from a unit of Hutchison Whampo Ltd, which is planning to sell $1.0 billion in debt in a global offering via Merrill Lynch & Co and Goldman Sachs & Co.

Other high-grade deals include FPL Group Inc's $450 million offering of unsecured bonds via JP Morgan & Co and Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc's $600-$750 million multi-tranche offering via Lehman Brothers.
Looming on the horizon is a mega-offering of $2.5 billion in debt via Raytheon Co, although sources said that deal is now likely to price later this month or early next.
Despite recent volatility in emerging debt markets, this week's junk bond calendar includes sizable amount of emerging market debt supply.

Morgan Stanley & Co is expected to once again attempt to price a deal from Brazilian utility company, Espirito Santo Centrais Eletricas SA (ESCELSA). ESCELSA plans to sell $350 million in Euro/144a senior unsecured notes due 2007.
Morgan postponed the offering last week due to volatility in the Brazilian debt markets.

Compania Internacional de Telecomuniciones SA (COINTEL) plans to sell $400 million in debt this week. The deal is expected to include seperate tranches denominated in U.S. dollars and Argentine Pesos.
Goldman Sachs & Co and Merrill Lynch & Co will co-lead manage the deal. COINTEL is the holding company for Telefonica de Argentina, the largest telephone company in Argenita.
Also, Autopistas del Sol SA, an Argentine toll-road company, plans to sell $150 million in notes due 2004 and $230 million in notes due 2009 via Citicorp Securities Inc.
